candidates.title: Indoor Positioning Datasets for Large Retail Spaces
candidates.shift: Academic work on RTT+RSSI fingerprint datasets is building the groundwork for GPS-grade indoor positioning inside large buildings, including big-box and warehouse formats.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: if indoor-positioning accuracy becomes standard, store layout, robot-fleet navigation and in-aisle wayfinding could all be redesigned around a positioning-first logic.
candidates.evidence: Paper describes an Android app systematically collecting RTT/RSSI fingerprint data for large-scale indoor navigation systems.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of infrastructure-layer tech (positioning) moving from lab dataset to potential store-operations backbone. If it matures, expect indoor robotics and wayfinding apps to require this as base infrastructure, similar to how GPS underpins outdoor logistics.
candidates.author: Brijeshkumar U. Patel, Kaushika D. Patel

candidates.title: Circularity Credit Gap in Building Material Declarations
candidates.shift: Standard Environmental Product Declarations obscure the real value of recycled content in materials like steel, revealing an absent standard: a circularity-specific metric layered onto existing LCA frameworks.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: could presage new certification or insurance categories that reward recycled-content construction materials, changing what developers/retailers are required or incentivized to specify.
candidates.evidence: Study proposes new circularity metrics to supplement standard EPD end-of-life (Module C/D) interpretations for green steel.
candidates.source: International Journal of Life Cycle Assessment
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of a category absence: circularity has no standardized declaration format yet. If resolved, expect construction material procurement and green-building certification to add circularity scoring as a routine line item.
candidates.author: Matthew Rumsa, Michele John, Wahidul Biswas et al.

candidates.title: Micro Public Infrastructure Reframed as Urban Interface
candidates.shift: A public restroom renovation in Guangzhou is being treated as designed civic architecture rather than utilitarian infrastructure, reframing small municipal buildings as branded urban touchpoints.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: a peripheral-geography (China) project setting a design standard for ultra-small public infrastructure — could migrate into transit-adjacent retail amenity design elsewhere.
candidates.evidence: NODE Architecture & Urbanism renovated a public restroom at a bus terminal in Guangzhou's Dongshankou district as an 'open urban interface.'
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of reframing utility infrastructure as designed civic/commercial space. If this spreads, expect ordinary micro-infrastructure near stores (transit stops, restrooms, waiting areas) to be treated as brand and placemaking opportunities.
candidates.author: 韩爽 - HAN Shuang

candidates.title: Gulf Mixed-Use Towers Setting Vertical Retail-Office-Residential Scale
candidates.shift: Dubai's newly leased 93-story mixed-use tower continues a pattern of Gulf cities setting scale precedents for combined retail, office and residential vertical development.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: peripheral-geography megaprojects (Gulf) are effectively prototyping mixed-use vertical retail integration ahead of Western markets — worth tracking as a leading indicator, though already a named building.
candidates.evidence: Pelli Clarke & Partners' 358m, 93-story mixed-use tower completed construction and launched leasing in Dubai's Trade Centre First district in June 2026.
candidates.initial_analysis: Already a named, counted megaproject — included as context/Trend. The structural question worth watching is whether Gulf-scale mixed-use vertical retail integration becomes an exportable design template.
candidates.author: Antonia Piñeiro

candidates.title: Adaptive-Reuse Ordinances Unlocking Office-to-Housing Conversion
candidates.shift: LA's adaptive-reuse ordinance plus a new historic-landmark designation is enabling conversion of a 1970s brutalist office building into apartments — a policy-enabled pathway for obsolete commercial stock.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: signals municipalities pairing landmark status with code flexibility to solve office vacancy, a template that could later apply to dead mall or big-box retail real estate.
candidates.evidence: KFA plans to convert a brutalist Sherman Oaks office building into housing under LA's newly adopted adaptive reuse ordinance.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of policy catching up to physical obsolescence: from strict use-zoning toward flexible adaptive-reuse code. If widespread, retail landlords with struggling big-box or mall assets could gain similar conversion pathways.
candidates.author: Ben Dreith

candidates.title: Reclaimed-Material Wildlife Infrastructure as Land-Use Asset
candidates.shift: A wildlife tower built almost entirely from reclaimed farm materials treats biodiversity infrastructure as a formal land-use output, not decoration.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: could foreshadow retail/logistics sites being required or incentivized to build multi-species habitat structures under emerging biodiversity net-gain rules.
candidates.evidence: Pearce+ built a reclaimed-material wildlife tower for bats, owls, kestrels and invertebrates at Honeygar Farm, Somerset, as part of wetland restoration.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of land-use shifting from purely productive/commercial to regenerative multi-species use, driven by biodiversity policy trends. If this becomes codified (biodiversity net gain requirements), large retail/logistics parcels may need designed habitat structures on-site.
candidates.author: Tom Ravenscroft

candidates.title: Extreme Micro-Apartments as Affordability Provocation
candidates.shift: A developer built a 1.9m² apartment to literalize what a young adult can afford, using architecture as advocacy that could shape future minimum-size housing debates.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: if extreme micro-units gain traction as messaging or product, it reframes density expectations near urban retail sites and could drive demand for ultra-compact-format stores.
candidates.evidence: Riksbyggen and BBDO Nordics designed three flats sized to what a 25-year-old can afford to buy in Sweden, the smallest measuring 1.9 square metres.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of housing-affordability crisis being visualized through built form as protest/marketing. If normalized, expect debates about minimum unit sizes and ultra-dense urban infill near commercial corridors.
candidates.author: Cajsa Carlson

candidates.title: Adobe Revival as Low-Carbon Vernacular Construction
candidates.shift: Architects reviving dilapidated adobe structures for new residential builds in Latin America signals renewed legitimacy of vernacular, low-carbon construction methods outside standard code paths.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: a peripheral-geography construction method regaining traction could inform low-carbon building codes elsewhere, relevant to future low-cost/low-carbon store construction choices.
candidates.evidence: Colar studio revived an adobe structure into a new home (Casa Estelí) in Chiapas, Mexico, combined with new brick volumes.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of vernacular material revival driven by low-carbon construction pressure. If codified as a standard method, retailers building in hot/arid peripheral markets could adopt similar low-embodied-carbon approaches.
candidates.author: Starr Charles

candidates.title: Bio-Waste Streams Entering Material Design Pipeline
candidates.shift: Student design projects turning traditional-medicine waste, fish parts and mycelium into lighting and materials point to a growing supply of novel bio-waste feedstocks for physical products.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: an early-stage material substitution pipeline, currently academic-only, that could eventually feed low-carbon store fixtures and finishes if scaled commercially.
candidates.evidence: Politecnico di Milano school show features lighting from organic Chinese medicine waste and materials sourced from salmon bones/skin and mycelium.
candidates.initial_analysis: An example of speculative-to-real material innovation pipeline stage. If any of these bio-waste materials scale past academia, expect novel low-carbon fixture/finish categories for retail interiors.
candidates.author: Dezeen staff

candidates.title: Bio-Based Adhesive Absence in Construction Supply Chain
candidates.shift: Petroleum-based adhesives remain embedded throughout construction (drywall, furniture, packaging labels) with no mainstream sustainable substitute yet at scale.
candidates.ai_read: Tentative: a 'green adhesive' category doesn't yet exist at scale; if it emerges, it could ripple through building material specs, green-certification requirements, and packaging supply chains.
candidates.evidence: Researchers highlight petroleum-based adhesives used throughout construction, furniture and packaging, and describe efforts toward sustainable substitutes.
candidates.initial_analysis: An absence signal: a ubiquitous construction/packaging input has no green substitute standard. If resolved, expect new material specification categories and possibly insurance/cert implications for buildings and packaging alike.
candidates.author: Stephanie M. McPherson, SM ’11
